topics.title: Do plants breathe? Cellular respiration and gas exchange

concepts.learning_objective: Define cellular respiration and respiratory substrates and explain why energy is released stepwise and stored as ATP.
Explain how plants meet their gas-exchange needs through stomata, lenticels and air spaces without respiratory organs.
Describe the site, discoverers and sequence of reactions of the EMP pathway.
Identify the steps of glycolysis that use or form ATP and NADH + H+ and calculate its energy yield.
Describe how pyruvic acid is converted to ethanol or lactic acid and the enzymes involved.
Explain the low energy yield and hazards of fermentation and their consequences.

topics.title: Aerobic respiration: link reaction, TCA cycle and ETS

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA in the mitochondrial matrix.
Trace the reactions of the Krebs' cycle and the points where CO2, NADH, FADH2 and GTP are formed.
Explain the electron transport system, the role of oxygen and ATP synthesis by ATP synthase.
Calculate the theoretical net ATP gain per glucose and evaluate the assumptions behind it.
Compare fermentation and aerobic respiration in breakdown of glucose, ATP yield and NADH oxidation.
Identify the points at which fats and proteins enter the respiratory pathway.
Explain why the respiratory pathway is considered amphibolic rather than catabolic.
Define respiratory quotient and state its values for carbohydrates, fats and proteins.
Calculate RQ from a balanced equation or gas-exchange data and interpret the substrate used.
